audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert. 


Mentre i mercati tradizionali sono chiusi per il fine settimana, analizziamo gli ultimi sviluppi. 
Il Nikkei ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.38%, Shanghai in aumento dello 0.11%. 


Sul fronte dei mercati occidentali, nella seduta di nella seduta precedente, S&P 500 in rialzo dello 0.29%, VIX in aumento dello 0.59%, 
DXY in rialzo dello 0.13%, US 10Y Yield in calo dello 0.27%, oro in aumento dello 0.65% a 4644.5 dollari l'oncia, 
petrolio in calo del 5.12% a 108.17 dollari. 


Nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi. 


Tra le notizie, spiccano le tensioni geopolitiche con dichiarazioni su possibili interventi militari e 
le conseguenze sulle materie prime. Inoltre, l'accordo commerciale UE-Mercosur. 


Passando agli asset digitali, Bitcoin quota 78,379 dollari in calo dello 0.35%. 


Restiamo in attesa per l'evoluzione dei mercati nella prossima settimana.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin si mantiene sopra i settantottomila dollari, con una variazione del +0,16%. I flussi ETF hanno registrato un afflusso di 629,8 milioni di dollari. Questo movimento arriva mentre il Senato ha superato un ostacolo importante per il Clarity Act, che potrebbe influenzare positivamente il settore. 
  Tra le altcoin, Ethereum guadagna lo 0,35%, arrivando a duemilatrecento dollari, Solana cresce dello 0,24% a ottantatre virgola novantasei dollari, e BNB aumenta dello 0,36%, toccando i seicentodiciassette virgola novantadue dollari. 
  Il Fear & Greed Index è a 47, in territorio neutrale. Questo livello suggerisce cautela tra gli investitori.

Sui mercati attendiamo i dati economici in uscita. Per approfondire, trovate gli articoli sulla nostra piattaforma nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en:
Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. 

While traditional markets are closed for the weekend, let's analyze the latest developments. 
The Nikkei closed up 0.38%, Shanghai up 0.11%. 

On the Western market front, in the previous session, S&P 500 up 0.29%, VIX up 0.59%, 
DXY up 0.13%, US 10Y Yield down 0.27%, gold up 0.65% to $4,644.5 per ounce, 
oil down 5.12% to $108.17 

No major macroeconomic data out today. 

Among the news, geopolitical tensions stand out with statements on possible military interventions and 
the consequences on raw materials. Furthermore, the EU-Mercosur trade agreement. 

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin quotes $78,379 down 0.35%. 

We remain waiting for the evolution of markets in the next week.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin remains above seventy-eight thousand dollars, with a variation of +0.16%. ETF flows have recorded an inflow of $629.8 million. This movement comes as the Senate has overcome an important obstacle for the Clarity Act, which could positively influence the sector. 
Among altcoins, Ethereum gains 0.35%, reaching $2,300, Solana grows 0.24% to $83.96, and BNB increases 0.36%, touching $617.92 
The Fear & Greed Index is at 47, in neutral territory. This level suggests caution among investors.

On the markets, we await the economic data out. For more details, find the articles on our platform in the Top Stories section. Thanks for your attention and see you tomorrow.

articles.title: How to Win a Trade War: Book launch and discussion with Bown and Keynes
articles.snippet: Please join us online for a discussion with Soumaya Keynes and Chad P. Bown on their new book How to Win a Trade War, available for pre-order. Trade wars are here to stay, and refusing to engage in the fight is no longer an option. President Donald Trump's tariff announcements can crash markets and sour decades-long alliances. China's export restrictions on rare earths could bring the West's car production to a crashing halt. Curbs on trade in cutting-edge chips could determine who wins the artificial intelligence (AI) race. From identifying supply chain vulnerabilities to installing…

articles.title: The EU-Mercosur trade agreement is finally happening
articles.snippet: After more than 20 years in the making, the interim trade agreement between the Mercosur countries (Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay, and Uruguay) and the European Union finally applies provisionally as of May 1. This creates a trade area with around 700 million consumers, facilitating investment, trade, and cooperation. In addition, it is a clear geopolitical signal that these two blocks want to deepen their ties through a transparent, legally binding agreement. What will the effects of the agreement be economically and politically? Why was it so hard to agree, and what comes next? Is this an…

articles.title: Russia’s Oil Revenues Surge as the World Scrambles for Supply
articles.snippet: Following the Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022, several major world powers introduced strict sanctions on trade with Moscow. Europe and the United States have been gradually decreasing their dependence on Russian gas and other energy products and putting pressure on other countries to do the same, to place a financial strain on Moscow, as the war with Ukraine continues. However, some countries, such as India and China, have used these sanctions as an excuse to buy discounted crude and gas from Russia, in a bid to reduce costs and boost energy…

articles.title: Hormuz Deadlock Persists as Trump Faces War-Powers Deadline at Home
articles.snippet: Two months after the Iran war began, the Strait of Hormuz remains severely restricted for tanker traffic while U.S. President Donald Trump faces a key legal deadline at home under the 1973 War Powers Resolution. As of early Friday, May 1, the deadlock at the world’s most vital oil chokepoint, the Strait of Hormuz, doesn’t appear close to being resolved. The U.S. is doubling down on the naval blockade outside the Strait aimed at stopping Iranian oil exports. But Iran controls most vessel movements through the lane and is increasingly…
